title: Imperatives and directions
grammarNote: ИМПЕРАТИВ (повелительное наклонение) — это форма глагола, которую используют для команд, советов, инструкций и указания маршрута. Образуется из БАЗОВОЙ ФОРМЫ глагола без подлежащего. Отрицание: Don't + base verb. Смягчённая форма: Please + imperative.

grammarTable.subject: Affirmative (+)
grammarTable.example: Turn left. · Go straight. · Cross the road. · Take bus 14.

grammarTable.subject: Negative (−)
grammarTable.example: Don't turn right. · Don't miss the stop. · Don't be late.

grammarTable.subject: Polite request
grammarTable.example: Please show me your ticket. · Please be quiet in the library.

grammarTable.subject: Let's (we both)
grammarTable.example: Let's walk — it's not far. · Let's take the metro!

grammarTable.subject: Advice / Warning
grammarTable.example: Make sure you book early! · Remember to check your ticket!

grammarTable.subject: Sequential steps
grammarTable.example: First, turn left. Then cross the road. Finally, go straight.

rows.example: Go straight ahead for about 300 metres.
Turn right at the traffic lights.
Cross the road at the zebra crossing.
Walk past the old bank building — don't enter it.
Take the first left after the roundabout.
Follow the road for 500 metres until you see the park.
The pharmacy is on your left, just after the café.
The bus stop is directly opposite the library.
It's next to the post office, between the bank and the café.

rows.form: It's at the end of the road.
rows.example: Keep going — it's right at the end of the road.
It's on the corner of Lenin Street and Park Avenue.
There's a huge sign — you can't miss it!
Excuse me, where is the nearest bus stop?

rows.form: Could you tell me how to get to...?
rows.example: Could you tell me how to get to the train station?

rows.form: Am I going the right way for...?
rows.example: Am I going the right way for the city centre?
How far is it? — About 10 minutes on foot.

rows.form: Is there a bus / metro / tram?
rows.example: Is there a bus that goes to the museum?

rows.form: Can you point me in the right direction?
rows.example: I'm lost — can you point me in the right direction?
✅ Turn left here. (No subject in an imperative!)
✅ Turn left at the lights. (Base verb, not -ing!)
✅ Cross the road here. (No "to" before imperatives!)
✅ Don't be late! (Never 'to' after Don't!)

grammarTip:
Последовательность направлений в английском:
First, ... → Then, ... → After that, ... → Finally, ...

Пример: First, go straight for 200 metres. Then, turn left at the roundabout. After that, cross the road. Finally, you'll see the museum on your right.

💡 Запомни: You can't miss it! = это очень легко найти (невозможно не заметить)
💡 'It's on the corner' vs 'at the corner' — оба варианта верны в британском English.

exercises.text: ___ straight ahead past the traffic lights.
exercises.hint: Imperative = base verb only. No subject, no -ing, no "to".

exercises.text: ___ the road at the zebra crossing — it's safer.
exercises.hint: Imperative: Cross + noun. Base verb, no additions.

exercises.text: ___ the first exit — take the second one.
exercises.hint: Negative imperative = Don't + base verb. Never 'Don't to take'.

exercises.text: "Turning left at the roundabout" is a correct direction.
exercises.hint: Directions use the imperative: "Turn left." Not "Turning left."
Let's + verb = a suggestion for both people. Let's take the metro!

exercises.instruction: Put in the correct sequence word.
exercises.text: ___, go straight. ___, turn right at the junction.
exercises.hint: Sequence: First... Then... After that... Finally...

exercises.instruction: Which polite direction question is correct?
exercises.text: Choose the best way to ask for directions.
opts: Excuse me, could you tell me where the post office is?
Tell me where is post office.
exercises.correct: Excuse me, could you tell me where the post office is?
exercises.hint: Polite: Excuse me, could you tell me...? — formal and respectful.

exercises.instruction: Which sentence describes a landmark correctly?
opts: It's on your left, next to the café.
exercises.correct: It's on your left, next to the café.
exercises.hint: "on your left" ✅ "next to" ✅ — correct preposition usage.

questions.text: Which is a correct imperative direction?
questions.hint: Imperative = base verb (Turn). No subject, no -ing, no "to".

questions.text: ___ right at the roundabout, then go straight.

questions.hint: Don't + base verb = correct negative imperative.

questions.text: "Let's walk — it's not far" is a suggestion for both people.
questions.hint: Let's = Let us → suggestion including the speaker.

questions.text: "Please ___ your boarding pass at the gate."
How do you politely ask for directions?
opts: Excuse me, could you tell me where the station is?
questions.correct: Excuse me, could you tell me where the station is?
questions.hint: Polite: Excuse me, could you tell me...?

questions.text: "Walk past the bank" uses the correct imperative form.
questions.hint: Walk (base verb) + past (preposition of movement). Correct imperative!

questions.text: Which word correctly puts steps in order?
questions.hint: First, go straight. Then, turn left. After that, cross the road.

opts: It is very difficult to find
It is very easy to find — very obvious
questions.correct: It is very easy to find — very obvious
questions.hint: "You can't miss it" = it is so obvious/big that you will definitely see it.

questions.text: The pharmacy is ___ your left, ___ to the bus stop.
questions.hint: "on your left" + "next to" — correct prepositions for position.

questions.text: Which describes the location of a place correctly?
opts: It's in corner of the street.
It's on the corner of the street.
questions.correct: It's on the corner of the street.
questions.hint: "on the corner of" = correct English expression.

questions.text: "Don't to turn right" is correct English.
questions.hint: Don't + base verb (no 'to'!). Correct: Don't turn right.
Opposite = directly facing, on the other side of the road.

questions.text: ___ the road, then ___ left — the museum is right there.
Which sequence is correct for giving directions?
questions.hint: Correct order: First → Then → After that → Finally.
